transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Thanks for coming in. I'd like to go through your medication first, then work, then sleep and mood. What are you taking at the moment?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Sertraline. I started it in the spring.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: And what dose is that?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: One hundred milligrams each morning. I began on fifty and my GP doubled it after a month.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Do you ever miss a dose?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Yes. Three or four times a week I forget the morning tablet, usually on days when I leave early.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Were you on anything else before the sertraline?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Citalopram, twenty milligrams, for about a year. It did nothing for me, so I stopped it last winter.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Any side effects from the sertraline?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Some nausea in the first fortnight. It has gone now.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Do you take anything else regularly?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Two vitamin D tablets in the morning and one magnesium tablet at night. That's all.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Okay. Let's turn to work. What's your role?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: I lead an engineering team. About ten people report to me, though the number shifts a bit.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Has the team changed in size this year?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: It was six people in January and now we're at eleven, because two contractors joined last month.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: How long have you been in the role?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: I took over in March of last year, so about eighteen months now.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Is there anyone helping you manage them?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: No deputy, no. It's just me, which is part of the strain.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: How many hours are you working in a week?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Around forty-seven and a half, if I add up the evenings.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: That's a lot. Now sleep. How much do you get on a work night?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: About 4.7 hours, according to my watch.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: How often do you wake in the night?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Most nights, two or three times, then I lie there thinking about the rota.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: And your mood?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Low a few days a week. Mostly Mondays and Tuesdays, when the planning meetings are.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Have you had any thoughts of harming yourself?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: No, nothing like that.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Is there anything you want to add?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: The tablets help a bit, I think, but the workload is the real problem.

assessment.label: Medication
assessment.text: Takes sertraline 100 mg each morning. Was previously on citalopram 40 mg. Misses the morning dose almost every day. Takes four supplement tablets a day in total. Reports no side effects.

assessment.label: Work
assessment.text: Manages a team of ten engineers. The team grew from six to nine people during the year. Has led the team since March this year. Works about 47 hours a week. Has no deputy.

assessment.label: Sleep and mood
assessment.text: Sleeps 4 hours on a work night. Wakes in the night every night. Mood is low a few days a week. The sertraline has resolved the low mood. Denies thoughts of self-harm. Meets criteria for major depression.
